patterns.pattern: Entities are scoped to contexts such as channel, region, or customer for segregation and configuration.
patterns.example_phrasing: A cart (or order) is specific to a sales channel, region, and customer.

patterns.pattern: Access to sensitive or administrative features is limited to authorized personnel or user roles.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only authorized users (like admins) can access sensitive customer or sales data.

patterns.pattern: A customer may only have one active cart or order session at a time.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only one active shopping cart per customer session is allowed.

patterns.pattern: All sensitive data, especially payment and personal information, must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
patterns.example_phrasing: All credit card and customer data is encrypted (HTTPS, database).

patterns.pattern: Checkout requires complete required information before proceeding to payment or completion.
patterns.example_phrasing: Checkout requires addresses, shipping, and payment to be provided first.

patterns.pattern: Product and content visibility is configurable per channel, region, or group.
patterns.example_phrasing: A product can be shown or hidden from particular channels or customer groups.

patterns.pattern: Order information (such as line item price) is fixed at creation and unaffected by later product changes.
patterns.example_phrasing: Price of an order does not change if the product's price is updated afterward.

patterns.pattern: Inventory reservation is atomic and prevents overselling at time of order confirmation.
patterns.example_phrasing: Inventory is reserved when the order is confirmed, to prevent double selling.

patterns.pattern: Customers must agree to terms and conditions before purchasing, if this is enabled.
patterns.example_phrasing: Customers must accept terms before completing checkout.

patterns.pattern: Guest checkout is available (checkout without registering an account).
patterns.example_phrasing: Guest checkout is possible; registration is optional.

patterns.pattern: Product categorization is hierarchical; every product belongs to at least one category in the tree.
patterns.example_phrasing: Products are organized in nested categories and must belong to at least one.

patterns.pattern: Store credits, gift cards, or vouchers are tied to specific customers and are non-transferable unless otherwise specified.
patterns.example_phrasing: Store credit belongs to a customer and can't be transferred.

patterns.pattern: Operations affecting financial balance or discounting (gift cards, store credit) must be atomic and consistent.
patterns.example_phrasing: Gift card adjustments are atomic and cannot lose balance if updated concurrently.

patterns.pattern: Access to preview or special content (e.g., streaming movies) is limited to users who own or are eligible for it.
patterns.example_phrasing: Customers can only access streaming if they purchased it and are within viewing window.

patterns.pattern: Updates to user or product profile information do not retroactively affect existing or past orders.
patterns.example_phrasing: Changing an address in the customer profile does not change the shipping address for existing orders.

patterns.pattern: System must support high availability and disaster recovery.
patterns.example_phrasing: System supports backup, failover, and >99.99% uptime.

patterns.pattern: Only specified frontend environments are supported for proper operation.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only validated browsers and OS environments are supported.

patterns.pattern: All business-critical actions (such as order confirmation) must occur before subsequent dependent steps (such as shipping).
patterns.example_phrasing: Order confirmation is required before shipping.

patterns.pattern: Only registered customers may use certain advanced features (e.g. reordering, storing payment methods, streaming).
patterns.example_phrasing: Only registered customers may purchase digital goods or access account-based features.

patterns.pattern: Core data (e.g. customers, orders) should be retained/maintained even after account cancellation, unless explicitly deleted.
patterns.example_phrasing: Customer data is stored after the account is canceled, unless deleted by admin.
